specification.title: The connection is terminated inside a nested scope that then fails
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Write the marker `outer`, and make sure the write was sent.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure the write was sent.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report the backend PID. The runner sees the savepoint's subtransaction lock. The runner then terminates the backend, and waits until it has gone.
Wait settle_ms, then raise an application error in the nested scope; its ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails on the closed connection.
The outer scope catches the nested scope's error.
Checkpoint `after-outer`, after the outer transaction's API has returned: report the same backend PID. The runner records whether that session is still inside a transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If the API reports that the outer transaction committed, PostgreSQL committed it, with the outer scope's writes and none of the failed nested scope's writes.
When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.

execution.description: Django's documented default: transaction.atomic() for the outer transaction and a nested transaction.atomic() for the savepoint, PostgreSQL backend, psycopg 3, CONN_MAX_AGE 0, no connection pool. TX-03 is not run in this mode. The default closes the database connection at the end of each request (not-applicable-by-design for handing a transactionally active connection to later work). https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.1/ref/databases/#persistent-connections

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: Inside the nested scope, after its write, before the framework's savepoint rollback.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and the whole transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: Connection errors for the savepoint rollback and for anything after it.

knowledge: The framework sees its connection fail during the savepoint rollback.

api_outcome.basis: atomic() returned without raising; rollback() raised and Atomic.__exit__ dropped the connection
api_outcome.contract: Django documents transaction.atomic() as: "If the block of code is successfully completed, the changes are committed to the database. If there is an exception, the changes are rolled back." Atomic.__exit__ commits only when exc_type is None and needs_rollback is false; otherwise it rolls back (django/db/transaction.py). A savepoint rollback that raises django.db.Error sets needs_rollback and does not replace the original exception. A root rollback that raises django.db.Error is swallowed and connection.close() is called. An exception that is not django.db.Error is not caught, so needs_rollback stays false. The DatabaseError admonition says: "After such an error, the transaction is broken and Django will perform a rollback at the end of the atomic block." Model.save uses mark_for_rollback_on_error, which sets needs_rollback when a database error is raised inside an atomic block.

error.message: application error: the nested scope fails

evaluation.reason: TX-02.1 held: the API reported: failed; xid 868 rolled back at report time (`after-outer`); outer visible: false; inner (failed scope) visible: false; TX-02.2 held: the session after the outer API returned: closed

preconditions.description: the write of marker "outer" had reached PostgreSQL at `outer-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "inner" had reached PostgreSQL at `inner-after-write` (a subtransaction lock, in pg_locks)
the runner terminated the backend at `inner-after-write`, and it had gone before the adapter resumed
the nested scope's error reached the outer scope, which handled it
the runner observed the transaction's session after the outer API returned
